use.title: 🚦 How to use this course
use.pact:
• One module per week (~10–12 h). Each one ends with a deliverable in a repo.
  • Tick a module's ✅ only when the deliverable works and you can defend it.
  • “I don't know” is fine; “I didn't try” isn't.
  • Everything goes into your portfolio — at the end you have real projects to show.
use.rulesTitle: Golden rules (my method · in my own words)
use.rules:
• “Shift your time from typing to deciding.”
  • “AI amplifies your judgment; it doesn't replace it.”
  • “Validate against the contract, don't bend the test to fit the response — a false green is worse than an honest red.”
  • “Certification is signed by a human; it's not a checkbox you automate.”
  • “Iterate narrow, confirm wide: fast on the details, rigorous at the close.”
  • “‘All green’ doesn't mean ‘the software is fine’ — it means my tests, as written, didn't find anything.”
  • “Test the tester, mutate reality: break the world on purpose and see if your suite screams.”
  • “Rules live in hooks and CI, not in prompts; evidence is command + hash + exit code.”

eval.title: How you're assessed · QA Automation Path
eval.intro:
QA Automation Path · Cristian Guerra

How you're assessed

This site has no server and no teacher grading for you. The assessment is yours, and it rests on evidence you can show: commands, hashes, screenshots and your repo. Here's the full rule. ← Back to the course

🧒 Explained like you're 8: every module has a short test that grades itself, a task with a list of “I did it if…” and a table with four levels, from “not yet” to “excellent”. You pass the module when the test goes well and the task reaches level 3.
eval.s01:
What every module includes

🎯 Objectives and prerequisites

What you'll be able to do when you finish, in verbs that can be checked, and what you need before you start.

📓 Short theory + 🧪 lab

Just enough theory and a hands-on lab. In the newer modules, the lab is a real public repo.

🧠 Self-grading quiz

8 random questions from the module's bank (between 8 and 18 per module), one answer per question and the explanation for each one. You pass with 6 out of 8. Every attempt draws different questions.

✅ Challenge with verifiable criteria

Criteria you check with a command or a screenshot, not with an opinion. Examples: “your suite kills at least 5 of 6 mutants and the JSON report includes hashes”, “your judge has a kappa ≥ 0.6 against your labels”, “a PR with a failure is blocked from merging”.

📏 4-level rubric

1 · Not met · 2 · Getting there · 3 · Passed · 4 · Outstanding. Level 4 in each module asks for something specific on top.

🧬 Mutation of the week

You break something on purpose in your own work and show that your check notices, or you publish that it doesn't. That's the WAR thread: test the tester.
eval.s02:
When you pass

A module: quiz ≥ 6/8 and challenge at level 3 of the rubric (all criteria met). Then you tick the deliverable's ✅.

The final exam: 26 scenario questions that cut across the whole course; you pass with 80 %.

The “WAR Audit” capstone: all four rows of the integrated rubric at least at level 3, and someone else reproduces your package in a clean environment with exit 0 and the same fingerprint.

Your progress, your best score on each quiz and your exam are saved in your Google account if you sign in with it, or only in this browser (localStorage) if you continue as a guest. When you sign in, whatever you did as a guest is added to your account.
eval.s03:
What counts as evidence and what doesn't

Counts as evidenceDoesn't count
✓ Yes: the exact command, its output and its exit code, saved as they came out.✗ No: “it worked for me”, or a screenshot without the command that produced it.
✓ Yes: a SHA-256 or a fingerprint that someone else recomputes and gets the same.✗ No: a log that exists but that nobody can tie to the run that produced it.
✓ Yes: the order in git log: preregistration, then data, then results.✗ No: a threshold that moved after seeing the score, even if the new one “makes more sense”.
✓ Yes: a control that must pass and another that must fail, with both results.✗ No: a green suite you never saw fail.
✓ Yes: a hypothesis that failed, published with its number.✗ No: deleting the hypothesis that failed or changing the criterion so it passes.
✓ Yes: someone else's reproduction, published as is, even if it comes out different.! Careful: your own reproduction on another machine of yours, or one operated by an assistant, counts as “reproduced”, not as “reproduced by a third party”. Say so under Limits.
eval.s04:
How to check your own criteria

  • Order in time: git log --reverse --format="%h %ad %s" --date=iso.
  • Thresholds untouched: git log -p -- thresholds.json shows no changes after the first run.
  • Exit code: end every command with ; echo "exit=$?" and save the output.
  • Hashes: shasum -a 256 archivo, or shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS for a list.
  • Fingerprint in two environments: a CI job with a matrix that runs grep -q "fingerprint: XXXX-XXXX-XXXX", like predictor-debugger's verify.yml.
  • Clean environment: a fresh CI runner or a container that's born and dies with the command, for example docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/w -w /w python:3.12-slim python3 verificar.py.
eval.s05:
Each module's rubric

1 · Not met2 · Getting there3 · Passed4 · Outstanding
The deliverable is missing or doesn't run.It runs, but fails at least one passing criterion.Meets all the passing criteria.Meets everything plus the extra that module asks for.

The newest modules come with a rubric by axes: four rows, each one with these four levels. There, passing means having all four rows at least at level 3.
eval.s06:
Integrated rubric for the “WAR Audit” capstone

One row per course axis, plus the evidence. Passed = all four rows at least at level 3.

Axis1 · Not met2 · Getting there3 · Passed4 · Outstanding
AI-assisted QAThe assistant ran without a log, or the rules live only in the prompt.There's a session log, but commands, exit codes or hashes are missing, or the hook has no attack suite.A hook or gate with an attack suite in CI (exit 0); receipts.jsonl with every command, exit code and SHA-256; the diff reviewed by a person and a Co-Authored-By trailer on the assistant's commits.On top of that, a blind double review (two reviewers who can't see each other's work and a scoped fixer) and a “What was not executed” section.
Mutant executionNo mutants or no baseline.There are mutants, but the kill rate counts infrastructure or baseline failures, or the ledger is missing.At least 6 mutants as data, with one change each; a valid baseline; a kill rate that can be recomputed from the JSON; every SURVIVED in the ledger with its cause; a strict mode that fails on the survivor.On top of that, the ledger prioritizes the next run and there's a blind round with a hash commitment verified with shasum -a 256.
WAR ParadigmOnly the product is tested, never the guards.A single guard is tested (the suite or the judge).At least two different guards are tested (suite, judge, hook, gate or evidence verifier), each with a control that must pass and another that must fail, with its command and exit code.On top of that, a guard that failed (a survivor or a false green) is published, along with what changed afterwards, without moving thresholds.
Evidence and reproductionClaims without a command that produces them.Partial evidence, preregistration after the data or a fingerprint that differs between environments.Preregistration before the data; a lockfile and --locked or npm ci; the same fingerprint in CI and on your machine; someone else reproduces in a clean environment with exit 0 and the same fingerprint; a README with Limits and What would contradict me.On top of that, the person reproducing has no connection to the project, uses another operating system and their report is published as is, with the differences they found.
eval.s07:
The path

The full path has 35 modules. The numbers below are the ones on the course map.

Complete, from scratch: all 35 modules in order, about 37 weeks at 10–12 h per week.

20 weeks, if you already automate UI or API tests. Each card says which module to work on that week.

12 weeks: weeks 1 to 5 as in the 20-week path (modules 01, 08, 10, 14 and 15); week 6, modules 21 and 02 together; then 19, 24, 25, 27 and two weeks for 28 (preregistration, controls, fingerprints and reproducibility). Modules 29 to 33 stay as a scientific QA elective, and the capstone, for when you finish.
eval.s08:
Honesty

Nobody checks your answers from a server. If you tick a ✅ without evidence, the only person you're fooling is yourself. The course's rule applies here too: a green only counts if you know it would have come out red when something was wrong.
